texts: When an apprentice's solo count is large, the Council invests the apprentice as a Keeper.
When a lantern of an apprentice fails, that apprentice's solo count resets.
When an apprentice's lantern dims, that apprentice's solo count resets.

fields.sentence: When an apprentice's solo count is large, the Council invests the apprentice as a Keeper.
parse: (: apprentice_invest_rule (Implication (And (Member $x apprentice) (Member $c solo_count) (Possession $c $x) (Member $c large)) (And (Member (sk_invest $x) invest) (Agent (sk_invest $x) sk_council_1) (Patient (sk_invest $x) $x) (Member (sk_keeper $x) keeper) (Experiencer (sk_keeper $x) $x) (Member $x keeper) (Result (sk_invest $x) (sk_keeper $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q2_gaps: Predicative "as NP" complement of a transitive verb ("invests the apprentice as a Keeper"): the instruction set names no encoding for "V NP as NP" — the resultative State-result shape is defined for AP results ("painted it red") and for intransitive change-of-kind ("turned into a museum"), so the parse's transfer of that shape to an as-phrase is an extension rather than a licensed form.

"Whenever / when P, Q" rule whose trigger clause P is COPULAR ("when an apprentice's solo count is large"): the machinery mandates tying the per-occurrence Skolem response to its trigger with During, but a flat copular premise yields no event witness to anchor it, and a whenever-trigger is not among the listed state-reification triggers — the instruction set does not say which way to resolve this, and the parse silently drops the During link.
review.notes: Routing, possessive genitive (Possession, possessed first), singular collective "the Council" as a non-distributing role-filler with no Name atom, and the 1.0/0.9 rule TV all follow the instruction set; the two gaps above are construction coverage, not mis-assertions.

fields.sentence: When a lantern of an apprentice fails, that apprentice's solo count resets.
parse: (: when_lantern_fail_reset (Implication (And (Member $e fail) (Patient $e $l) (Member $l lantern) (Possession $l $a) (Member $a apprentice)) (And (Member (sk_solo_count $a) solo_count) (Possession (sk_solo_count $a) $a) (Member (sk_reset $a) reset) (Patient (sk_reset $a) (sk_solo_count $a)) (During (sk_reset $a) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The response event is Skolemized on the apprentice — (sk_reset $a) — instead of on the trigger occurrence $e, so every failure of that apprentice's lanterns derives one and the same reset event During each of them, losing the per-occurrence reading the whenever machinery specifies.

review.notes: Everything else conforms: indefinite participants route the bare 'when P, Q' to the whenever rule, the of-genitive and the 's-genitive both take Possession (a lantern and a count are not parts of a person), solo_count gets its genus with the non-predicable modifier unexposed, and 'fail'/'reset' take Patient as change-of-state undergoers. Keying the count itself on $a is right — only the event key is at issue.

issues.reason: The whenever machinery keys the response on the trigger occurrence, and a dependent existential must be "a Skolem function of every universal that scopes over it", so (sk_reset $a) collapses every failure of that apprentice's lanterns into one and the same reset event asserted During each distinct failure — a falsehood the per-occurrence key would avoid.

adjudication.defect_summary: Key the response on the trigger: (Member (sk_reset $e) reset) (Patient (sk_reset $e) (sk_solo_count $a)) (During (sk_reset $e) $e) — or (sk_reset $e $a) as a function of both universals — while the count itself correctly stays (sk_solo_count $a).
adjudication.notes: Everything else conforms: the indefinite participants route bare "when P, Q" to the whenever rule, both genitives take Possession (neither a lantern nor a count is part of a person), solo_count gets its genus with the non-predicable modifier unexposed, and fail/reset take Patient as change-of-state undergoers.

fields.sentence: When an apprentice's lantern dims, that apprentice's solo count resets.
parse: (: apprentice_lantern_reset_rule (Implication (And (Member $x apprentice) (Member $y lantern) (Possession $y $x) (Member $e dim) (Patient $e $y)) (And (Member (sk_reset $x) reset) (Member (sk_solo_count $x) solo_count) (Possession (sk_solo_count $x) $x) (Patient (sk_reset $x) (sk_solo_count $x)) (During (sk_reset $x) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Both genitives take Possession (neither possessed item is a component), "that apprentice" correctly reuses the premise variable, the per-apprentice solo count is a dependent Skolem function, and dim/reset both give their internal-change-of-state subjects Patient; solo_count exposes only the head genus since "solo" fails the predication test.
